title: revlens comment round
description: docs/comments/<round>/<round>.json in the engagement repository: one round of reviewer comments and how each of them was settled. The file name repeats the directory name, which is how the adapter finds it.

id.description: Short id of the round, e.g. K2

role.description: The reviewer's role; the viewer shows its first sentence on the comment card

received.description: Local wall-clock time the round arrived

reviewed_version.description: Version of the document the reviewer read

source.description: Where the comments came from - an e-mail, Word comments, minutes

id.description: Comment id; a change log entry mentioning it in this form becomes a comment resolution

scope.description: Chapter ids the comment is about

title.description: One line, used when there is no summary

source_section.description: Where in the source the comment sits - paragraph, chapter, page

verbatim.description: The comment as the reviewer wrote it, never rewritten

summary.description: What the comment claims, in the processor's words

check.description: The first gate: is the comment factually right?

decision.description: The second gate: is it accepted?

at.description: Date, or a local wall-clock time

resolution.description: The third gate: how far it was actually worked into the text. A comment can be confirmed and accepted and still not worked in, and only this says so.

changes.description: What was done, one line each. A chapter file named here joins the comment to the commit that touched it.

at.description: When it was worked in. Compared against the baseline date to decide whether the comment is in scope at all.

answer.description: What was sent back to the reviewer
